text: Bank trouble: A big bank is failing and people are pulling their money. You are president — you:

answers.text: Guarantee everyone's money and put public money into the bank.

pros: Stops panic fast; people keep access to their savings.
cons: Costs the government a lot; seen as bailing out rich bankers.

answers.text: Guarantee small savers only; let big investors lose money.

pros: Protects ordinary people while punishing big risk-takers.
cons: If private rescue fails the problem could spread anyway.

answers.text: Do nothing — let the bank go bankrupt and follow court rules.

pros: No taxpayer money used; firms learn to be careful.
cons: Could cause big job losses, panic, and credit problems.

answers.text: Freeze money leaving the country and take over the bank temporarily.

pros: Stops money fleeing and lets you fix the bank properly.
cons: Scares investors and may hurt ties with other countries.

text: Factories failing: Local factories are closing because of cheap imports. You:

answers.text: Put taxes on those imports and give local factories money to keep running.

pros: Keeps people employed and buys time for factories to adapt.
cons: Goods may cost more and other countries might retaliate.

answers.text: Pay for job training and help people move to new jobs; keep trade open.

pros: Helps workers learn new skills while avoiding long-term market harm.
cons: Expensive and slow; not everyone will adapt quickly.

answers.text: Save only truly important firms; otherwise let the market decide.

pros: Focuses help where national interest needs it.
cons: People argue about which firms are 'important'.

answers.text: Lower taxes and rules to attract foreign factories and buyers.

pros: Can bring new investment and jobs.
cons: May not help current workers fast enough; community decline.

text: Big budget hole: The budget is short. You:

answers.text: Raise taxes on the richest and keep social programs.

pros: Protects services and helps the poor.
cons: Wealthy may invest less; political fights.

answers.text: Cut non-essential spending now and borrow a bit.

pros: Quick fix without big fights.
cons: Some useful programs might suffer.

answers.text: Cut most public programs and try to boost business growth.

pros: Encourages private growth and long-term efficiency.
cons: People who need help suffer right away.

answers.text: Make a one-time wealth tax and get a loan from abroad with conditions.

pros: Raises money quickly; may modernize systems with loan conditions.
cons: Foreign loan rules can be unpopular and seen as interference.

text: Machines take jobs: Automation will cut many jobs soon. You:

answers.text: Pilot a basic income and fund retraining programs.

pros: People have a safety net and can retrain for new work.
cons: Very costly; debate about work incentives.

answers.text: Give tax breaks to companies that keep or retrain workers.

pros: Encourages firms to keep staff and invest in training.
cons: May keep inefficient firms afloat.

answers.text: Let the market shift jobs naturally; cut red tape for new industries.

pros: Faster innovation and new job types.
cons: Big short-term hardship for displaced workers.

answers.text: Take over big tech firms to control how automation is used.

pros: You can direct tech to serve social goals.
cons: Risk of bad management and less private innovation.

text: Rents are exploding: City protests are growing. You:

answers.text: Cap rent increases and build lots of public housing.

pros: Immediate relief for renters and calmer streets.
cons: Developers may build less; long-term supply issues.

answers.text: Give tax breaks to private builders who make affordable homes.

pros: Faster building using private money.
cons: May favor profit over real affordability.

answers.text: Make it easier to build more homes and relax zoning rules.

pros: More housing supply should lower prices over time.
cons: Short-term disruption and gentrification risks.

answers.text: Give poor renters direct vouchers to pay rent.

pros: Targets help to the worst-off fast.
cons: Needs steady funding and political support.

text: After an attack: Terrorists hit the capital. You:

answers.text: Give security big new powers to watch and detain suspects.

pros: Could stop more attacks quickly.
cons: Hurts privacy and can be abused.

answers.text: Pass temporary, narrow powers that need court approval.

pros: Balances safety with rights.
cons: Slower response; powers may be extended.

answers.text: Use community programs and better police-community work.

pros: Builds long-term trust and prevention.
cons: Slower to stop immediate threats.

answers.text: Tighten borders and restrict movement in certain areas temporarily.

pros: Immediate containment of cross-border risks.
cons: Stigmatizes communities and can strain diplomacy.

text: Artist controversy: An artist offends many and crowds protest. You:

answers.text: Defend the artist's freedom; say the government won't censor art.

pros: Protects free speech and creativity.
cons: Upsets some groups and may cause more protests.

answers.text: Allow only clearly illegal content to be restricted; mostly defend speech.

pros: Limits real harm while keeping debate open.
cons: It can be hard to define what is harmful.

answers.text: Set rules that public broadcasts must follow national standards.

pros: Calms protests and keeps public order.
cons: Risks soft censorship and less creativity.

answers.text: Break up protests and arrest instigators to stop unrest.

pros: Restores order fast.
cons: International criticism and chilling effect on dissent.

text: Drug trial: A city decriminalized drugs; crime dropped but ER visits rose. You:

answers.text: Expand decriminalization nationwide and increase health services.

pros: Reduces arrests and focuses on health.
cons: More short-term health costs and need for services.

answers.text: Decriminalize but limit some drugs and boost rehab centers.

pros: Balanced health-first approach.
cons: Needs funding and trained staff.

answers.text: Go back to stricter rules while testing treatment programs.

pros: Addresses public concerns about safety.
cons: More arrests and possible black markets.

answers.text: Let each city choose its own approach.

pros: Local solutions can match local problems.
cons: Different cities will get different results.

text: Refugee wave: 200k people flee across your border. You:

answers.text: Open borders for now and start programs to find them work.

pros: Big humanitarian help and potential new workers.
cons: Large short-term cost and pressure on services.

answers.text: Take limited numbers, focus on the most vulnerable and skilled.

pros: Helps those most in need while limiting burden.
cons: Many people will still be left without help.

answers.text: Put people in guarded camps and process claims slowly.

pros: Controls flows and reduces hasty integration.
cons: Poor conditions and humanitarian criticism.

answers.text: Close the border; give aid across the border only.

pros: Protects domestic resources short-term.
cons: Human cost and international backlash.

text: School book fight: A new history book skips bad events to boost pride. You:

answers.text: Reject the book; require balanced history that includes tough parts.

pros: Teaches truth and critical thinking.
cons: Angers some nationalists and can cause backlash.

answers.text: Use a modified book that adds context but keeps unity messages.

pros: Middle ground that calms both sides.
cons: Neither side fully happy.

answers.text: Let local areas pick their own books.

pros: Local fit and innovation.
cons: Uneven education quality across regions.

answers.text: Approve the pride-focused book to boost unity now.

pros: Short-term calm and unity.
cons: Hides truth and harms credibility later.

text: Neighbor coup: A friendly country is taken over by a junta. You:

answers.text: Lead a group of countries to sanction the junta.

pros: Pressures the junta without sending troops.
cons: Sanctions can hurt ordinary people.

answers.text: Help rebels secretly and prepare targeted strikes on leaders.

pros: Could remove the junta quickly with less open war.
cons: Dangerous if exposed; moral and legal risks.

answers.text: Keep trade and deal with the junta to avoid conflict.

pros: Keeps business going and avoids war.
cons: Looks like accepting a coup; reputational costs.

answers.text: Send humanitarian aid and push for monitored elections only.

pros: Helps people and keeps diplomatic options open.
cons: May be seen as too weak by some at home.

text: Trade fight: A partner undercuts your exporters with cheap subsidy. You:

answers.text: Take it to the trade body and if needed hit them with tariffs.

pros: Shows you defend local business and use rules.
cons: Could raise prices and start a trade conflict.

answers.text: Give temporary help to your exporters and try quiet diplomacy.

pros: Shields local firms while fixing the issue quietly.
cons: Costly and may only delay the problem.

answers.text: Find other markets so you aren't stuck with that partner.

pros: Long-term safety from one country's pressure.
cons: Slow to build and needs investment.

answers.text: Negotiate sector by sector and accept small deals for now.

pros: Avoids shock and may get gradual wins.
cons: Might not stop the damage quickly.

text: UN peace mission: UN asks you to lead troops to help a failing country. You:

answers.text: Lead a full mission with troops to protect civilians.

pros: Big chance to stop suffering and raise your country's standing.
cons: Expensive and risky for your soldiers.

answers.text: Send training and equipment but no combat troops.

pros: Helps without big danger to your troops.
cons: Might not be enough to stop the crisis.

answers.text: Decline and focus on diplomacy and sanctions.

pros: Avoids casualties and big costs.
cons: People may keep suffering and criticize us.

answers.text: Join only if we get economic or trade benefits in return.

pros: Helps your economy while contributing to peace.
cons: Seems self-interested and could hurt legitimacy.

text: Cyber attack: Infrastructure is hit and things stop working. You:

answers.text: Strike back in cyberspace to destroy the attacker's tools.

pros: Sends a strong message and may stop more attacks.
cons: Risk of escalation and mistakes.

answers.text: Publicly blame them, impose sanctions, and fix our systems.

pros: Shows resolve and improves defenses.
cons: Slow response and attackers adapt.

answers.text: Quietly fix systems and talk privately to the attacker's government.

pros: Avoids public panic and open war.
cons: Might not stop future attacks.

answers.text: Treat it like a crime: investigate and arrest suspects where possible.

pros: Uses law and avoids open conflict.
cons: May be insufficient against state-backed attacks.

text: Great power pressure: Big powers want military bases; they offer money and support. You:

answers.text: Accept a base with clear limits to get security support.

pros: Immediate security help and military support.
cons: Less independence and possible political backlash.

answers.text: Refuse bases; instead build local defense pacts with neighbors.

pros: Keeps independence and builds local trust.
cons: Harder to build fast security.

answers.text: Take aid and investment, but stay militarily non-aligned.

pros: Money for development without committing troops.
cons: Could be seen as playing both sides.

answers.text: Declare neutrality and ban foreign military bases.

pros: Maximum independence and no foreign bases.
cons: Could be left vulnerable if threats rise.
